visual_action: A fast-paced animated video styled after a Spotify Wrapped summary. It uses bold graphics and text on alternating black and white backgrounds to present a year-in-review for "Media Bias Offenders." The video displays a series of statistics and lists, culminating in a ranked list of news organizations deemed "top offenders," including The Washington Post, Reuters, MSNBC, The New York Times, and The Associated Press. It ends by showing photos of two Washington Post journalists, Alex Horton and Ellen Nakashima, before cutting to black and white footage of the White House.

on_screen_text.text: We're ready for you, Media Bias Offenders
You spread fake news. We listened!
Taste like yours can only be defined one way: SAD!
You complained for THIS many minutes!
Since you were into complaining from Day One. Your opinion isn't very popular.
1 The Washington Post Published an unsubstantiated lie to undermine the DOW's anti-terrorist ops.
2 Reuters Falsely reported that DOGE had disbanded- It's still saving taxpayers hundreds of millions.
3 MSNBC Demonized the National Guard after two servicemen were shot, one being killed.
4 The New York Times Claimed President Trump is incapable of fulfilling the duties of the Presidency based off of incomplete evidence.
5 The Associated Press Omitted vital context to push their own anti-Trump agenda.

spoken_summary: The audio consists entirely of a high-energy electronic music track with stylized vocal samples that are not decipherable as words.
audio_music: A continuous, upbeat, and funky electronic track ('Mercy' by Cosmonkey) with chopped vocal samples plays throughout the video, giving it a modern, fast-paced, and mocking tone consistent with the parody format.
editing_pacing: The video is a fast-paced slideshow with quick cuts between different animated text and graphic slides.
central_claim: Major news organizations are biased "media offenders" who spread fake news and push an anti-Trump agenda, and their work amounts to obsessive, unpopular complaining.
intended_effect: To discredit mainstream media outlets and specific journalists, encouraging viewers to see them as biased and untrustworthy purveyors of 'fake news.'
uncertainty_flags: The specific entities referred to by the acronyms 'DOW' and 'DOGE' in the on-screen text are unclear from the video's context.
